subject.title: [Bug]: Chrome extension browser relay removed with no cross-machine  replacement (regression)

question: Should OpenClaw restore a secure cross-machine Chrome extension relay path, expose a browser backend/plugin API for it, or keep the old relay retired?
rationale: The remaining work is not a narrow schema repair because it requires choosing the remote browser-control security model, user-consent surface, plugin/core boundary, and supported managed-hosting workflow.

options.title: Design secure plugin/backend API
options.body: Define a browser backend or plugin contract for remote relay implementations with explicit user consent, scoped access, action logging, and upgrade-safe configuration.

options.title: Restore core relay behind policy
options.body: Bring back a core-supported extension relay only if maintainers accept the security boundary and require fresh-install plus upgrade proof for remote hosts.

options.title: Keep relay retired
options.body: Document the retirement and supported host-local alternatives, accepting that managed remote-host extension workflows remain unsupported in core.

recommendation.title: Design secure plugin/backend API
recommendation.body: Define a browser backend or plugin contract for remote relay implementations with explicit user consent, scoped access, action logging, and upgrade-safe configuration.

likelyOwner.reason: The original relay, replacement path, and heavy browser-area history make this the clearest available routing candidate for the product/security decision.
